methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Series B → next-stage step-up multiplier (1.9x) to $129M total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.rationale: Median across 3 same-sector + same/adjacent-stage peers in Climate & Energy. Range: $700M - $3.0B.

public.rationale: Public-co frontier-tech comp in Climate & Bio-Manufacturing

data.narrative:
INERATEC is a Series B climate and energy company that has raised $129M to date. Our valuation analysis draws on two primary methods triangulated against a peer set of three same-sector, same/adjacent-stage companies: KoBold Metals ($3.0B), Electric Hydrogen ($1.0B), and Amogy ($700M).

The stage-progression method applies a 1.9x step-up multiplier typical of Series B advancement, yielding $245M. The peer-median approach references the $1.0B median valuation across the three comparable companies, with a stated range of $700M to $3.0B. These two methods produce meaningfully different outputs, reflecting both the heterogeneity within climate-tech venture outcomes and the sensitivity of early-stage valuation to peer selection and growth assumptions.

Triangulating across both methods supports a valuation range of $208M (low) to $1.1B (high), with a median of $623M. The wide spread reflects key uncertainties: the ultimate commercialization trajectory of INERATEC's technology, capital intensity of scaling, and competitive positioning relative to peers at more advanced stages. The peer-median method anchors to observable Series C valuations, while stage-progression relies on historical step-up patterns; neither method fully captures technology-specific risk or market timing. A mid-range valuation of approximately $600M–$700M balances both approaches.
